header_summary:
The Time-Shifted Proof of Work (TSPOW) proposal introduces a novel approach to enhance the stability, security, and decentralization of cryptographic mining. By decoupling the mining and block authorship processes and introducing mining warrants that follow a Gamma distribution model, TSPOW significantly reduces the variability in block production times. This adjustment not only stabilizes block-time variance but also counters selfish-mining strategies by making withholding of proofs economically disadvantageous, thereby promoting a fairer distribution of mining opportunities and reducing the dominance of large mining pools. The full proposal, including specifications and security analysis, is detailed in the draft Bitcoin Improvement Proposal available at [Full spec and analysis](https://github.com/corepool/timeshiftpow).

The SHRINCS Working Group has introduced a draft for a new cryptographic scheme that offers compact and quick verification signatures, presenting it as a semi-stateful solution potentially resilient against quantum threats. Despite being in the prototype stage and requiring comprehensive peer review, SHRINCS promises enhanced security and efficiency with its public keys and signatures optimized for applications like the Lightning Network. However, the scheme's stateful nature necessitates sophisticated management to prevent security vulnerabilities. Further details and community feedback opportunities are outlined at [SHRINCS.md](https://github.com/SHRINCS/shrincs-bip/blob/main/SHRINCS.md).

A critical denial-of-service vulnerability in Core Lightning (CLN), a Bitcoin Lightning Network node implementation, was identified, demonstrating how specific message handling in `connectd` could lead to out-of-memory conditions and node crashes. The resolution involved modifying message handling to incorporate a backpressure mechanism, significantly mitigating the risk of unchecked resource consumption. This fix, which underscores the necessity of robust system design in cryptocurrency networks, is documented in [PR 8525](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/pull/8525).

recent_posts.title: Draft BIP for discussion: Time-Shifted Proof of Work (TSPOW) — an informational consensus-design proposal
recent_posts.summary:
- TSPOW stabilizes block-time variance by separating warrant accumulation from block production.
- It mitigates selfish-mining by making withheld proofs economically unviable and employing a transparent selection algorithm.
- The decentralization is enhanced by selecting block authors from a matured pool of warrants, reducing large pool dominance.

recent_posts.title: SHRINCS: an efficient hash-based signature scheme for Bitcoin (first draft)
recent_posts.summary:
- The SHRINCS Working Group has presented a new draft BIP introducing a hash-based signature scheme.
- SHRINCS features include compact keys, faster signature verification, and post-quantum security.
- The scheme requires review and includes limitations like management software for the state counter.

recent_posts.title: Disclosure: Crashing CLN with a flood of pings
recent_posts.summary:
- A DoS vulnerability in Core Lightning could let attackers crash nodes by overloading memory.
- Modifications were made to how `connectd` manages message processing to prevent crashes.
- The fix involves a backpressure mechanism to control memory usage and enhance system security.

recent_posts.summary: - The analysis compares jewelry theft statistics to wrench attacks and associated costs.  - Securing Bitcoin oneself is costlier than securing physical valuables like jewelry.  - The recommendation is to avoid risky and non-transparent security methods for assets.

active_posts.summary: - BIP 324's upgrade aims to mitigate quantum threats to Bitcoin's encryption.  - Debates continue on adopting hybrid or purely post-quantum key mechanisms.  - Implementing quantum-resistant BIP 324 is simpler than consensus-layer changes.
